root_cause.text: An off-by-one error in the loop condition within `nvme_dbbuf_set()` caused iteration beyond the last valid queue index, leading to an out-of-bounds access when `dev->online_queues` was used as an inclusive upper bound instead of an exclusive one.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `for (i = 1; i <= dev->online_queues; i++)` to `for (i = 1; i < dev->online_queues; i++)`, and the CVE description states that valid indices are 0 through `dev->online_queues − 1`. The KASAN report shows a slab-out-of-bounds read at an address 244 bytes past the allocated region, consistent with accessing the element at index `dev->online_queues`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in nvme_dbbuf_set loop to avoid accessing an out-of-bounds queue array element.
intent_record.what: Changed the loop condition from `i <= dev->online_queues` to `i < dev->online_queues` in the nvme_dbbuf_set function.
intent_record.how: The loop now iterates one fewer time, stopping before accessing the queue at index `dev->online_queues`, preventing an out-of-bounds array access or freeing an invalid queue.
